name: The Winterhold City
description: Winterhold, a city of the winter elves, lies by the delta of the Humming Gulf. Each manor showcases the Kemet style of architecture, complete with Gothic spires and towers that overshadow ornate courtyards. Their stone facades are adorned with shadowed alcoves and intricate ironwork, making these elegant yet harrowing manors serve as fortresses for various clans. On the streets, a blend of elves and undead can be seen, with the undead performing most of the menial work in the city. At night, undead servants carrying lanterns cast ghostly glows, creating eerie shadows on the columns and turrets of surrounding buildings. The only sounds are the dragging of bony feet and the fluttering wings of crows, mixed with the waves crashing along the coast. Currently, the city is in turmoil due to mysterious murders. Dead bodies are found at night, marked with disturbing Kemet symbols. Rumors are circulating about a possible Kemet spy, winter elf clan disputes using the Kemet name as a pretext, or even a scheme of the Cult of Shadow Wing. Compounding the unease, some undead have begun showing signs of defiance, alarming the city’s nobility. The noble houses are seeking aid to investigate these issues, but so far, they remain unresolved. Another problem is a political struggle against the conservatives in the Republic’s parliament. A decade ago, it became common for winter elves to pay for the right to animate a person’s body as a mindless undead after death, a practice necessary to maintain their number of servants. They assert that the soul of the deceased is free to journey into the afterlife; however, many in the Republic are apprehensive about this practice, raising concerns about potential assassinations, exploitation of the impoverished, and violations of sacred burial rites. The winter elves argue that a body is merely an object, and that individuals have the right to sell their bodies post-mortem. With the looming threat of Kemet naval forces, lawmakers on both sides are desperate to find common ground, understanding that this issue must not fracture their unity.
